X.note: Half the frame is flat blue sky. Large empty green plain. The rock is a decent hero object but small and distant. The town is a barely visible sliver. Only one tiny troop block and a few stray posts. Long straight walls and trenches look like untextured primitives. Smoke is faint and doesn't read as a siege. Nothing in the frame says the line is occupied or a battle is under way.

Y.note: Lower camera angle and better composition. Rock sits left of centre, sea on the right, and the town with its church tower is visible on the spit. Many regiment blocks fill the foreground and lead the eye toward the walls and the rock. Smoke drifts across the middle distance, which adds some atmosphere. But the troops are black cylinder grids on gold slabs, which reads as toy blocks or a Lego parade rather than soldiers. The foreground blocks are repetitive and cropped, and the pale smoke looks like flat sprites. There are no guns, no ships, and no human-scale detail.

why: Y has a stronger composition with a dense, readable besieging army, sea and town in view, and smoke. X is mostly empty sky and grass with almost no troops.
top_fix_for_weaker: Lower the camera and push in on the isthmus. Fill the plain with many troop columns, gun batteries, tents and campfire smoke. Cut the sky to about 25% of the frame. Add depth with foreground props such as gabions and cannons, and shift the walls and rock into a clear diagonal composition.
top_fix_for_better: Replace the cylinder-grid regiments with varied soldier figures in red or blue coats. Break up the uniform blocks with columns, officers, cannons, gabions, tents and ships in the bay. Add warm directional light and volumetric cannon smoke to get away from the toy look.
